target_customer: Manufacturers, distributors, retailers and logistics providers in Morocco and the MENA region that run their own fleets or hire carriers
problem: Companies in the region managed shipments with spreadsheets and disconnected tools, with little visibility across departments, ERP systems, in-house fleets and third-party carriers.
business_model: B2B SaaS transport management system sold by subscription

founders.name: Mehdi Cherif Alami
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists no history. TechCrunch (2022-02) says the two founders together previously worked in consulting and logistics at McKinsey, PwC, OCP Group and Strategy&, without attributing employers to each person.

founders.name: Omar El Kouhene
prior_employers: Freelance logistics consultant and shipping broker
education: Maths and Info preparatory classes, Lycee Sainte Genevieve
founders.background_notes: Details from the YC company page. Described as Founder there and as CPO by TechCrunch and Wamda.

competitors.name: Trella
competitors.what: Egyptian marketplace and brokerage connecting shippers with trucks

competitors.name: ShipBlu
competitors.what: Egyptian e-commerce last mile and fulfillment company named as a regional peer

competitors.name: Flextock
competitors.what: Egyptian warehousing and fulfillment startup named as a regional peer

technical_complexity.rationale: A multi-module transport management system with routing algorithms, real-time tracking and ERP integration is standard enterprise software engineering with some hard parts such as routing and integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise TMS deployments integrate with ERPs and carrier workflows, which creates switching costs, but the product category is well known and global vendors like SAP exist. TechCrunch said regional SaaS tools for shipment flows were few and far between.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Freterium. By 2025 its site claims 100+ customers including large FMCG and retail brands.

market_need_then: In February 2022 TechCrunch reported that SaaS tools for managing shipment flows across departments and ERP systems were few in the region, and the company reported 20+ enterprise customers in its first full year and 35 percent monthly growth.

branding.domain_note: freterium.com redirects to freterium.ai as of 2026 (observed in a fetch); no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Current site uses the tagline The AI Transport Standard and the headline Beyond TMS

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found nothing about the name or identity. Only generic B2B positioning is visible; the brand is a B2B tool name with no sourced community or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Freterium is an active Casablanca company that raised a 4 million dollar seed round led by Partech in early 2022 and, by its own site in 2026, claims 100+ customers including large retail and FMCG names. It filled a regional gap for transport management software, helped by founders with logistics and consulting backgrounds. No later round, exit or shutdown was found.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch, Partech and Wamda; Jawlah says it closed in December 2021 and Persana dates it 2022-01-24, so 2022-02 is the announcement date. Aggregators list totals of 4.12M and 7.3M, unverified. Founding year varies (2017 to 2020) across sources; YC page says 2018. Trella, ShipBlu and Flextock come from the Feb 2022 article, about five months after the S21 batch. No Series A found.
